candidates.name: OS Terrain 5 Overview
verified_facts: OS Terrain 5 is a 5 m post-spacing DTM with full Great Britain coverage.
It is updated quarterly.
Published accuracy is 1.5 m RMSE in urban/major communication routes and 2.5 m RMSE in rural and mountain/moorland areas.
semantic_limits: Its metre-scale RMSE is too coarse to replace EA 1 m LIDAR for sub-metre parcel height-difference measurement.
Use only as a secondary landscape sanity check and gross-outlier detector.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 5 Technical Specification
verified_facts: OS Terrain 5 grid uses regular 5 m post spacing and is supplied in 5 km by 5 km tiles.
The GML coordinate reference system is EPSG:27700 British National Grid.
Grid and contour products come from the same source data.
semantic_limits: Format and CRS consistency do not increase the source vertical accuracy.
Tile-level interoperability evidence is secondary QA only.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 5 National Grid tiling
verified_facts: OS Terrain 5 is divided into 5 km by 5 km tiles identified from National Grid references.
National Grid references encode easting before northing.
semantic_limits: Tile identity is spatial addressing evidence and is not a height measurement.
Tile checks must not override exact parcel polygon and raster-pixel sampling.

candidates.name: National Grid and the OSGB36 TRF
verified_facts: OSTN15, together with ETRS89 OS Net coordinates, defines the National Grid.
OS documents relative accuracy values for OSGB36 control stations.
semantic_limits: Control-station accuracy is not terrain-height accuracy.
Horizontal reference-frame evidence must remain separate from vertical elevation uncertainty.

candidates.name: Coordinate reference systems
verified_facts: Coordinate transformation is required to move between coordinate reference systems.
OS states ETRS89 GNSS coordinates should pass through OSTN15 to become OSGB36 National Grid coordinates.
semantic_limits: CRS transformation correctness does not establish parcel-boundary identity or elevation accuracy.
Measurement joins remain native-grid-first and transformation-aware.

candidates.name: INSPIRE GML technical guidance
verified_facts: HM Land Registry data is captured against British National Grid.
The guidance identifies EPSG:27700 as the native British National Grid CRS for INSPIRE polygon use.
The guidance warns that reprojection to WGS84 can shift some features by up to 15 metres.
semantic_limits: WGS84 display coordinates must not be used for exact parcel containment when native EPSG:27700 geometry is available.
INSPIRE polygons remain indicative extents rather than legal boundary determinations.

candidates.name: Survey Data Catalogue - vertical accuracy of the LiDAR data
verified_facts: EA specifications require absolute height error below plus or minus 15 cm RMSE.
EA expects relative height random error to be no more than plus or minus 5 cm.
semantic_limits: These are survey/product error specifications, not a parcel-specific legal or engineering survey certification.
Relative-error specification is retained as an uncertainty input rather than treated as guaranteed per-pixel error.

candidates.name: Survey Data Catalogue - point density considered in the LiDAR programme
verified_facts: EA states a 1 m DSM survey point cloud averages at least 1 point per square metre.
50 cm corresponds to 4 points per square metre and 25 cm to 16 points per square metre.
EA warns DTM point density under vegetation can be lower than DSM point density.
semantic_limits: Point-cloud density is not the same as raster resolution.
Density evidence does not replace pixel-validity, nodata and polygon-mask checks.

candidates.name: Survey Data Catalogue - projection information
verified_facts: EA supplies survey data in OSGB36 British National Grid with elevations above Ordnance Datum Newlyn.
EA LIDAR Composite uses OSTN15.
EA states post-26 August 2016 surveys use OSGM15, while older time-stamped surveys require metadata-specific geoid identification.
semantic_limits: Historical surveys must not be silently mixed across geoid/transformation generations.
Projection and datum metadata are provenance controls, not a substitute for surface accuracy.

candidates.name: LIDAR Ground Truth Surveys
verified_facts: EA ground-truth surveys are independently surveyed elevation points used to verify timestamped LIDAR surveys.
Ground-truth points are documented at plus or minus 3 cm RMSE.
EA compares LIDAR with ground truth to assess RMSE, standard deviation and random error.
semantic_limits: Ground-truth accuracy applies to the validation points and does not make every parcel pixel plus or minus 3 cm accurate.
A ground-truth survey can age and has stated reuse limits, so survey date remains material.

candidates.name: National LIDAR Programme
verified_facts: The National LIDAR Programme provides 1 m elevation data for all of England.
Phase 1 blocks were captured between January 2017 and February 2023.
Repeat block surveys are assigned incrementing phase numbers and data is published through the Defra survey portal on an ongoing quarterly basis.
semantic_limits: Programme coverage does not imply every current composite cell has the same survey date.
Per-location metadata remains required to determine which survey contributed to a parcel.

candidates.name: Survey Data Catalogue - LiDAR data metadata
verified_facts: EA states index catalogues can be downloaded for its LiDAR products.
The catalogues include details such as the time of year when data was collected.
semantic_limits: Metadata availability is provenance evidence, not numeric elevation evidence by itself.
A parcel result still requires hash-backed source data and exact spatial joins.
